title: SNAP remains a large, heterogeneous national support system with distinct scale and household layers
source_unit: USDA ERS national SNAP program, participants, SNAP households, and research-summary context
geography: United States; state range where reported

average_benefit.unit: US dollars per participant per month

share_of_us_residents.unit: percent receiving SNAP in an average month

share_of_usda_food_assistance_spending.unit: percent of USDA food and nutrition assistance spending

observations.method: Official USDA ERS program-statistics summary; current national totals and averages, not a new microdata estimate.
observations.uncertainty: The participant average and monthly average benefit are not a household benefit amount; program-scale figures do not identify eligibility, take-up, administrative burden, adequacy, or household outcomes.
observations.subgroup: National SNAP participants and US residents receiving SNAP in an average FY2025 month.
observations.counterinterpretation: A large program or high participation rate can coexist with incomplete take-up, persistent hardship, or uneven access; spending is not proof of benefit adequacy.

denominator.unit: US states; state range excludes the national aggregate

highest_state_participation.unit: percent of state residents receiving SNAP in an average month

lowest_state_participation.unit: percent of state residents receiving SNAP in an average month

state_range.unit: percentage-point spread between reported highest and lowest state shares

observations.method: Official USDA ERS state participation-rate summary.
observations.uncertainty: The page reports the range but does not by itself identify the roles of need, eligibility rules, administration, labor markets, demographics, or take-up in producing it.
observations.subgroup: US states, summarized by reported participation-rate minimum and maximum.
observations.counterinterpretation: State participation differences are not a ranking of program performance or household security; they may reflect different populations and policy environments.

observations.period: FY2024; SNAP household composition and benefit distribution

denominator.unit: published percentage base among SNAP households

households_with_earned_income_children.unit: percent of SNAP households with children

maximum_benefit.unit: percent of SNAP households receiving the maximum benefit for household size

minimum_benefit.unit: percent of SNAP households receiving the minimum benefit

observations.method: Official USDA ERS description of FY2024 SNAP household characteristics and benefit distribution.
observations.uncertainty: These composition shares describe participating households and are not estimates for all eligible households; categories may overlap and the page's reporting definitions govern interpretation.
observations.subgroup: SNAP households overall, SNAP households with children, and households by reported income and benefit categories.
observations.counterinterpretation: A household with earned income is not necessarily food secure, and a household with no reported income is not necessarily without other resources or support.

observations.period: Research-summary context; study-specific periods and populations

denominator.unit: USDA ERS research summaries with study-specific denominators; no single pooled denominator

food_security_timing.value: food security deteriorates before receipt and improves afterward

benefit_change_context.value: past increases reduced food insecurity; later real-value decreases reduced food spending and raised food insecurity

countercyclical_link.value: participation tends to track unemployment and poverty

observations.method: USDA ERS synthesis of multiple studies with distinct designs, periods, populations, and outcomes.
observations.uncertainty: This is a research gateway rather than one pooled causal estimate; individual study denominators and identification strategies must be read separately.
observations.subgroup: Study-specific low-income households, SNAP households, and economic periods summarized by USDA ERS.
observations.counterinterpretation: The research summary does not show that every participation change or administrative exit produced the same food-security outcome for a particular household.

related_sources.claim: National SIPP transition and following-hardship context for SNAP receipt states.
Study-specific office-access mechanism; participation is kept separate from USDA program scale and food-security summaries.

boundary: This is current official USDA ERS program and research-summary context, not a new national causal estimate. It keeps scale, state range, household composition, benefit distribution, and research-summary patterns separate from NBER access studies and SIPP person-month hardship estimates. It does not establish benefit adequacy, same-household route burden, downstream security, trust, political action, or geopolitical consequence. The retrieval hash covers the committed source-specific layer.
